clues: This city spreads across rolling hills at the foot of a mountain chain. More trees shade its streets than in any other big city in the land.
Weather here can swing fast in the cold months. Warm gulf air brings spring-like highs, then Arctic air drops the nights into the teens.
Trains built this town, and trains won it the big job in 1868. That year, the state capital moved here for its fine rail links.
Martin Luther King preached in this city for years. He served as co-pastor of a church here with his dad from 1960 to 1968.
The laws of Georgia are made in this city. It is the state capital, and the state's largest city too.
